scope: Four-window exact-caller R139 placement diagnostic; no adoption

decision_rules.replication: median(g[w,allowed]) > 5 and g[w,allowed] > 0 in at least 3/4 windows
decision_rules.interaction_pp: d[w,p] = g[w,p] - g[w,allowed], p in split,colocated
decision_rules.placement_sensitivity: abs(median(d[w,p])) >= 10 percentage points and at least 3/4 d[w,p] strictly share its sign
decision_rules.interpretation: Without replication, placement effects do not explain the original slow tail. With replication, a qualifying interaction signals placement sensitivity only, not a scheduler mechanism or a runtime fix.
decision_rules.required_reporting: All 24 cases, four paired gaps at every placement, both interaction series, all metrics and correctness/health/archive/cleanup checks.
decision_rules.stopping: Exactly four complete clean windows; no retries, changed thresholds, excluded windows or data-dependent extra windows.

comparisons.interpretation: Descriptive four-window gates only. Without baseline replication, placement effects do not explain the original tail. No kernel cause or candidate adoption is assigned.

limitations: All 24 cases and all four same-boot stock-production windows are retained; no new formal performance ranking or adoption.
Same-window C/R136 ratios stay separate for each placement. Interactions are differences of these percentage gaps, in percentage points.
Fresh daemon per case and balanced order do not eliminate temporal variation. Four descriptive windows are not a mechanism proof.
Exact exec-cpu helper masks were exercised before timing; parent mask, launch argv, successful exit and daemon live identity are checked. No live caller mask or per-cycle migration evidence exists.

Daemon CPU delta is recomputed from process-clock snapshots. Original caller CPU provides a positive clock delta only, so no independent caller before/after reconstruction is possible; no tick fallback.
Daemon context switches are window-boundary counts, not per-operation traces or waiting durations. CPU and wall are not subtracted.

Guard assertions cover configuration/mount/production identity within each window; health/boot and exact input identities agree across windows. Raw host process identities are not separately archived.
Only one-method ADD/REMOVE is exercised; event_1, event_nomatch, user events, memory and integration remain outside this diagnostic.
